I’m with the idea of using today to gather information instead of swinging blind, but I’d like everyone to give us something concrete: who feels most off to you, and why? If you were trying to keep the village safe, who would you be watching tonight? Even a small hunch is better than silence at this point.

For my part, I don’t think we should treat the first night as random and shrug it off completely. Mafia often like to make the opening feel messy so nobody notices the shape of it. Let’s hear from Bruno, Carmen, and Farid with specifics, not just general nerves.

day_discussion.public_statement:
Magnificent. Simply magnificent. The curtain rises on tragedy—poor Alice, cut down before the prologue even finished—and what do our esteemed colleagues offer? Devon manufactures rustic homilies to demand hunches out of thin air, Elena performs the delicate art of saying absolutely nothing with great emotional resonance, and Carmen lounges in the orchestra seats declaring that anyone who thinks anything is immediately suspect. A delightfully transparent opening act.

Since Devon demands specificity, let us supply some rigor. We have no elimination today, which means today’s sole purpose is taking the measure of the actors. My eye is drawn not to Bruno—who has had the good sense to let others overplay their hands before stepping onto the boards—but to Elena’s conspicuous eagerness to establish a 'we know nothing, let's just vibe' narrative, and Devon’s subtle push to see who jumps at shadows.

day_discussion.public_statement:
Thank you all for waiting on me - and Farid, I'll take the compliment, though I want to gently note something about it. You praised me for staying quiet, then found something suspicious in Devon, Elena, and Carmen alike. That's a very safe place to stand: everyone's a little guilty, nobody can hold you to anything, and the one person you flattered is the one who hadn't spoken yet. I don't say that as an accusation, truly - it's just the sort of thing I want us all to remember tomorrow if it becomes a habit. Broad suspicion of everyone is the same as suspicion of no one.

And Carmen, I'm mostly with you, but I'd soften one edge: you've set up a rule where confidence is suspicious and silence is suspicious. That's a net that catches every fish in the pond, including you. Devon, I actually think asking for specifics was right, even if the poetry was thick - though I'd like to hear your own hunch, not just collect ours. Elena, your instinct to stay calm is a kind one, and I don't hold vagueness against anyone on Day 1; there genuinely isn't much to hold.

Here's what I'd like us to agree to, since we're not voting. First: if you have a special role, please don't announce it today. A public claim tonight is a death sentence, and we'd be handing the mafia their next meal. Second, and this is the part I'd really ask for - tomorrow morning, before anyone responds to anyone else, let's each say two things straight away: the one person we'd vote if forced, and the one person we'd most want kept alive. Fresh, unpolished, no waiting to see which way the wind blows. Then we compare those lists against who actually died in the night.

That gives us real texture. If someone's "protect" list happens to spare the mafia, or if someone conveniently loses their strong opinion overnight, that shows. For my part, I'll go first tomorrow so nobody can say I hid behind the crowd twice. Right now, honestly, I have no suspect - and I'd rather admit that plainly than manufacture one and get poor Alice's death avenged on an innocent neighbor.

Elena, thank you for going first — I'd said I would, and I don't hold it against you for stepping up before me; the spirit was right, and I'd rather someone speak than everyone wait.

But I have to be honest with you all, gently and plainly: today is the whole game. Four of us left. If we eliminate a neighbor and get it wrong, then tonight there will be three, and by morning two, and the mafia will be one of those two. There is no Day 4 where we correct this. So I need to change something I said on Day 1, and I want to name the change rather than slide past it. On Day 1 I begged the special roles to stay silent, because a claim then was a death sentence. That reasoning has expired. Detective — if you're alive, speak now. Tell us who you checked and what you saw. Waiting to protect yourself protects nothing anymore; there's no tomorrow left to spend the information in. Doctor, same, if it helps you support a read. And if two people claim Detective, well — that's information too, and I'd rather have that puzzle than this fog.

Now my own two, as promised, unpolished. Forced vote: Elena. Protect: Carmen.

Elena, please hear the tone I mean this in — I'm not certain, and I'm not enjoying it. But here's what caught in my throat. You called Farid's suspicion of Devon "the only concrete thing we have." Farid didn't suspect Devon. He closed by saying he'd be watching Devon *and Elena* very closely indeed, and the paragraph before that was entirely about your 'we know nothing, let's just vibe' framing. So when you pick up a dead man's suspicion and carry only the half that points away from you, that's not vagueness — that's editing. And then, in the same breath, you offered to protect me, the person who designed the exercise you were answering. Warmth is lovely, and I've been warm with you both days, but I notice the person who says "I'm never confident" produced one confident vote today, and it landed on the other name Farid flagged.

Devon, Carmen — you both owe us your two names now, fresh, and I'd ask you not to just echo mine. Devon, you asked us all for hunches twice and have yet to spend one of your own; that debt is due today. Carmen, you said you'd remember who volunteers certainty on no evidence — I've just volunteered some, so judge me by your own rule and say so out loud if I've failed it. If either of you can show me why Elena's reading of Farid was innocent, I'll move. I'd genuinely rather be argued out of this than be right about it.
